key_insight: An agent-guided multi-fidelity learning workflow can detect and correct numerical instabilities in GW-BSE excited-state calculations, yielding more reliable quasiparticle gaps and exciton binding energies without removing real strain effects.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster and more trustworthy high-throughput screening of optoelectronic materials, especially where expensive many-body simulations are prone to convergence failures or spurious artifacts.
method: Use a structural agent to flag fragile calculations and assign confidence weights.
Combine a small set of high-accuracy reference points with machine learning transfer across related strain, stacking, and k-point settings.
Apply Gaussian process corrections with calibrated uncertainty estimates to recover improved excited-state properties.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved agreement with higher-fidelity references than a no-agent baseline across stacking registries, strain branches, and reciprocal-space samplings.
watch_item: The approach depends on correctly identifying numerical fragility; if the agent misclassifies cases, corrections could underweight valid physics or miss hidden convergence issues.
paper_title: Agentic multi-fidelity learning of quasiparticle and excitonic properties
